title: BCG vaccine for newborns
what: A vaccine against tuberculosis. Your baby gets a small injection into the skin of the left upper arm, usually at the maternity hospital.
why: For newborns in the first days of life, unless there is a reason not to.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; the mark on the arm usually heals in 2 to 4 months
tell_doctor: If your baby was born early or with low weight
If your baby has health problems right now
If there are immune system conditions in the family
If anyone in the family has tuberculosis

prepare.title: Consent
prepare.text: At the maternity hospital, you will be asked to sign a consent form.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Ask the doctor if you want to know about reasons not to vaccinate.

prepare.title: If it was not given
prepare.text: If the vaccine was postponed at the hospital, it will be given at the clinic.

bring: Your baby's documents, if the vaccine is given at the clinic
steps: The nurse wipes the skin on the left upper arm
The vaccine is injected into the skin with a thin needle
A small white bump appears. It soon goes away
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
feel: After 4 to 8 weeks, a small lump or tiny pimple appears at the spot. This is normal
Then a scab and a small scar
after: Do not put anything on the spot or cover it
Do not touch or squeeze the scab
You can bathe your baby, just do not rub the arm with a washcloth
Show the scar to the pediatrician at a checkup
red_flags: A large sore over 1 cm at the spot, or very red skin around it
A swollen lump in the left armpit

faq.q: Is it normal to have a pimple on the arm?
faq.a: Yes, that is expected after a month or two. Do not treat it with anything.
That happens. Show the arm to your pediatrician, who will say what to do.

reminders.text: Your baby's BCG vaccine is tomorrow. Bring the documents and hospital discharge papers.
